claims.assertion: Human participants learn novel 3D finger-posture-to-2D avatar-endpoint relation with three controllable angles and originally generated external visual goal coordinates; no external controller's goal setter is part of human cognitive system.

Two researcher-imposed human start postures H1/H2 correspond to approximately identical avatar endpoint with distinct joint configuration; target landscape contains trained and withheld interpolation/extrapolation test goals.
claims.original_source: main pp3–5; Fig1–2; original S4 Fig

claims.assertion: Twenty included human subjects practice goal-oriented feedback 24 blocks of 80 seconds; test phases provide selected target cues and measure movement endpoints and kinematics without the same training feedback.

Human subjects learn task-dependent reach accuracy with feedback, demonstrate PCA low-dimensional synergies from posthoc 3DoF movement patterns; PCA is experimenter analysis not a verified trained explicit network implementation.

Integrated Goal Babbling uses feedback from actual attained sensory endpoint and goal to learn an inverse sensorimotor mapping in parallel with goal-oriented movement, rather than exhaustive premotor babbling only.

Agent simulation assumes the world's original forward kinematics f:q∈R3↦(x,y) 2D, implemented by external task; forward motor outcome function is not itself learned or inferred as agent internal forward predictor.

Original synthetic Goal Babbling agent updates a local linear inverse mapping g:(x,y)→q estimated by qhat; η=0.2 online fixed by engineer; this is not an independently emergent cognitive optimal planner.
Simulated learning uses a fixed experimenter-defined list of 40 goal targets each block; the source's model did not discover an arbitrary new goal objective from internal rewards.

Agent generates 24 linearly interpolated intermediate subgoals between successive externally sampled target points, producing 25 individual motor execution/update steps per training target, 1000 operations/block.

The action q(t) is current local linear inverse prediction qhat(x*,t) plus a slowly time-varying stochastic bounded exploratory deviation e(t) in three original motor joints; actual movement can differ from predicted inverse.
claims.original_source: main pp19–20 Eq3; Rolf 2012 borrowed Eqs6.8–6.10

claims.assertion: Source original motor outcome f(q(t)) is observed by the learner after executed exploratory action; inverse model adjusts based on goal/outcome reference and observed motor state, not on an unimplemented autonomous forward-model network.
claims.original_source: main p19–20 original algorithm and refs

claims.assertion: Training sequence repeats externally generated goals/subgoals and updates retained local linear inverse mapping across successive simulated trial actions; explorer noise evolves slowly; session/block temporal plots distinct from direct human neural adaptation inference.

Exploration generator and learner are borrowed source-specific Rolf/Steil/Gienger 2010–2012 goal babbling original and Rolf 2012 doctoral pp68 noise formulas; P20 manuscript supplies model identity/parameters but not exact full thesis-derived numerical equation source.

Two-phase Motor Babbling initially random exhaustive movement then training of sensorimotor inverse goal trajectories versus integrated Goal Babbling concurrent goal-directed outcome-guided exploration; observed human support is relative and source conditions bounded.

Original authors use 100 artificial agents evaluated for two start conditions and 20 human subject traces; original source explicitly calls comparison qualitative illustration, not a matched formal original statistical hypothesis that humans execute exact same algorithm.

Human observed source across-time performance improved; between starting-condition main p=.944 versus same-article S1 original table printed p=.44 conflict, each nonsignificant (not an exact single trustworthy p). Artificial agents original H2 early advantage is not reproduced in humans.
claims.original_source: Original PDF p8 primary source and exact original DOCX S1 table plus Fig2

claims.assertion: Artificial agent modeled H2 early acceleration, human no statistically significant between-condition learning-rate effect; source printed original human p=.944 body versus p=.44 same-article DOCX conflict both nonsignificant.
claims.original_source: Original main pp7–9, S1 exact publisher table, source Fig2 and separate S1 Fig

claims.assertion: Author experimenter measures each q1/q2/q3 variance and relative movement trajectories, not a direct inspection of actual learned neural inverse map; redundancy permits same 2D endpoint through different 3D joint solutions.

Both human and simulated groups can show ~90% total 3-joint movement variance captured by first two experimenter PCA principal components; measured dimension reduction not model proof of equal mathematical internal representation.

Human participants favor changes in original lower-endpoint-impact/less motor-sensitive joint patterns while simulated inverse model converges toward higher-effectiveness original first joint; average q2 human decrease is nonsignificant.
claims.original_source: main pp11–14 Figs6–7; supplemental original S2/S4 Tables

claims.assertion: Humans exhibit high initial motor variability declining during practice, whereas original agents start narrow motor exploration and spread it gradually as perturbations grow, source-reported cross-group difference.
claims.original_source: main pp13–15 Fig7; S3 Figure and S3 Table

claims.assertion: Observed human goal-directed learning supports integrated goal-related feedback but cannot exclude rapid motor-babbling within first training block, a competing exploration explanation.

Original artificial agent η=.2 fixed by source engineer; discussion suggests human learning-rate adjustment as POSSIBLE explanation only; no implemented agent intrinsic rate supervisor, no independent human η measurement.

Authors note alternate cost or reinforcement-driven motor exploration could in principle generate observed synergy/variance and cannot globally prove only source original Goal Babbling biological mechanism.
Agent outcomes depend on 3DoF geometry, task goal locations, fixed η=.2, original Rolf noise σ=.5 and σΔ=.005, subgoal interpolation plus initial H1/H2, not universal all robots or human brains.

Publisher original quantitative p-values, source reported response curves, participant PCA and synthetic trajectories are original published outcomes; no W4 fresh 20-person experiment or exact stochastic agent numerical reproduction.
